title: Shoreline reserved GPU & burst modeling sync
summary: Discovery call to size reserved GPU needs and validate Shoreline's isolation and burst requirements. Discussed traffic patterns (steady daytime inference with unpredictable nightly spikes), acceptable latency/SLOs, and trade-offs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC. SE walked through caching, continuous batching, and fallback strategies. Customer requested a cost model, a draft reserved capacity worksheet, and a short benchmark run with their 512-token completion workload.
transcript: [00:00] Avery: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Avery from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this. Marisol is my solutions engineer. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: Priya Rao, CTO at Shoreline. We run real-time clinical summarization and have a mix of inference and embeddings. Marcus is our SRE. Elena runs product ops.

[00:28] Marcus: Hey. Quick note — our current stack is a mix of k8s-hosted Triton for some models and the rest through the OpenAI API. We're trying to move away from public APIs for PHI reasons and get predictable unit cost.
[00:45] Marisol: Got it. Is the primary blocker compliance or cost predictability?

[00:50] Priya: Both. We need VPC or on-prem options for the more sensitive workloads, also reserved capacity to keep latency and cost predictable. We're also sensitive to night spikes from batch ingestion — unpredictable bursts up to 3x baseline.

[01:10] Avery: That makes sense. Today's goal is to map your traffic patterns, talk sizing for reserved GPUs, and discuss isolation (VPC / private) plus fallback playbook. We'll also sketch a benchmark plan. Sound good?
[01:24] Priya: Yep, go ahead.
[02:05] Marisol: Marcus, can you give a rough profile — qps, token lengths, percent of requests that are chat vs embeddings?

[02:13] Marcus: Baseline is about 120 qps across our main region during business hours. Average prompt + response is about 400 tokens, spikes push to 1.2k tokens. Embeddings are a smaller percent — maybe 15% of calls. Nighttime batch jobs can ramp effective concurrency to 370 qps briefly for 30–45 minutes when a partner backfill runs.

[03:00] Marisol: Ok so steady 120 qps with 3x short bursts. For sizing reserved GPUs we look at tokens/sec profiles and worst-case concurrent KV cache pressure. Do you have any sticky prefixes you cache?
[03:18] Priya: We do user-conversation prefixes, so KV cache hit rates are pretty good for repeaters but vary by tenant. Multi-tenant isolation is a hard requirement for regulated models.

[03:34] Avery: For multi-tenant isolation we recommend Dedicated reserved pools with node-level isolation (no co-mingling) and optional VPC peering for Private deployments. You could pin sensitive models to Private, and keep less-sensitive ones in Hosted dedicated — that's a common hybrid pattern.
[03:57] Elena: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private again? We've heard the terms but want clarification.

[04:03] Marisol: Short version: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for you in our environment with tenancy guarantees at the pool level; Private gives you a customer-controlled network and optionally an on-prem package—better for compliance like HIPAA.
[04:18] Elena: Ok thanks.
[05:45] Marcus: On SLOs: 95th percentile under 200ms is our goal for short completions, but for long 1k+ token runs we accept up to 1.2s p95. Can Redwood handle mixed latency SLOs?

[05:58] Marisol: Yes, we can route by policy. You can configure low-latency pools for critical paths and cheaper preemptible pools for background tasks. Also we can do model variants and automatic fallback to a quantized variant if a node is overloaded.
[06:22] Priya: What about bursting — how do you handle 3x spikes without overprovisioning for months?

[06:30] Avery: Two levers: reserved capacity sized for baseline plus short-term burst credits (we call burst capacity) and autoscaling with pre-warmed instances. For guaranteed isolation during bursts you can buy burst blocks that kick in and keep latency SLOs. For cost control, caching and continuous batching reduce per-token cost so you don't need as many GPUs as naive math suggests.
[06:52] Marcus: Is burst billed differently? We don't want huge bill shocks.

[06:57] Marisol: Yes bursts are metered; typical contracts include a buffer of included burst hours and overage rates. We'll share our reserved worksheet that models cost at various baseline-to-burst ratios.
[08:12] Priya: Can you do pre-warm so cold start doesn't blow our p95?

[08:18] Marisol: Absolutely — we support pinning warm replicas and pre-warm hooks. The trade-off is extra hourly cost vs avoiding tail latency. For your 200ms p95 target we recommend a small warm pool for short requests and a few higher-throughput nodes for long token runs.

[09:05] Avery: About security, you mentioned PHI. We have SOC 2 type II and can support SAML SSO, KMS integration for encrypted at-rest model artifacts, and audit logs for inference traffic. For on-prem we provide a deployable bundle and vpn/VPC peering guidance.
[09:28] Priya: We'll need written artifacts — can you send SOC 2 attestation and the private deployment runbook?
[09:33] Avery: Yes, we'll attach those to the follow-up.
[10:40] Marcus: A technical question — how does Redwood's KV cache behave under eviction during bursts? We worry about cache thrash causing latency spikes.

[10:50] Marisol: Cache eviction is LRU-based with a short-circuit fallback to recompute. We also support sticky routing so hot prefixes stay on the same node to keep cache hit rates high. During extreme bursts we can do graceful degradation and route background tasks to cheaper pools.
[11:22] Marcus: Any hard limits on maximum sequence length or throughput per GPU we should plan for?

[11:28] Marisol: Depends on model and quantization. For an fp16 70B model we usually get X tokens/sec numbers — but we'll run your 512/1k token workload in a quick benchmark. That will give concrete tokens/sec and p95 numbers for our infra.
[12:05] Priya: Benchmark — what do you need from us to run it?

[12:10] Marisol: A sample prompt set (representative prompts), preferred model, and preferred security mode (Hosted with customer data redaction vs Private). Preferably a small dataset, maybe 50–100 prompts covering average and spike cases.
[12:28] Elena: We can assemble that this week.
[13:05] Avery: On procurement timeline — are you looking at a Q2 commit or exploratory POC first?
[13:11] Priya: Likely POC first. We want a two-week bench/PoC with SLA targets and then a reserved capacity commit if numbers look good. Timeline target end of May for decision.

[13:34] Avery: Good. We'll propose a two-week PoC scope: reserved mini-pool + load test, VPC networking test, and an ops runbook. We'll also include pricing scenarios for baseline and 3x burst for a month and annual commitments.
[14:02] Priya: For the reserved sizing estimate — can you show a worked example?

[14:08] Marisol: Sure — rough calcs: baseline 120 qps * 400 tokens average = 48k tokens/sec system-wide; converting to tokens/sec per GPU depends on model; if we assume 50k tokens/sec per A100-class equivalent for your chosen model, baseline could be covered by 1–2 GPUs with caching/batching, but spikes to 370 qps push you to 4–5 GPUs unless we use burst credits and pre-warms. We'll produce a conservative and an optimized plan in the worksheet.
[15:01] Marcus: That 50k tokens/sec per GPU number — is that for fp16 or quantized?

[15:07] Marisol: That's an fp16-ish baseline. Quantization to int8 or int4 can give different profiles and lower latency but sometimes raises small quality regressions; we can test that in the benchmark.
[15:46] Priya: We also have tenant isolation concerns — can you pin GPUs per tenant?

[15:52] Marisol: Node-level pinning is available with Dedicated; you can also do per-tenant model pinning so specific tenants only hit private pools. For strict regulatory tenants we'd recommend Private with your own network controls.
[16:20] Avery: A note on rollout: common pattern is start with Hosted Dedicated for non-PHI traffic, then migrate regulated tenants to Private once audits and connectivity are green.
[16:39] Elena: Who from Redwood will run the benchmark and be our contact?
[16:43] Avery: Marisol will run bench and be primary SE contact. I'll own commercial and procurement.
[17:05] Priya: Cost — can you give a rough monthly number for baseline vs baseline+burst? We're trying to compare to our current spend on OpenAI plus Triton infra.

[17:14] Marisol: We'll put numbers in the worksheet. Ballpark: baseline reserved pool + moderate warm buffer often ends up lower than pure s3-ish cloud on-demand usage when you include caching. But exact depends on tokens and memory footprint. We'll provide TCO scenarios.
[18:50] Marcus: Instrumentation — what observability do you expose? We need token-level cost, per-tenant latency, and per-route dashboards.
[18:58] Marisol: Console has token-level breakdowns, tracing hooks, per-route SLO dashboards, and audit logs. We can also ship metrics to your existing Datadog/Prometheus via exporters.
[19:35] Priya: Any gotchas with Private on our side — network, storage, or key management?
[19:41] Avery: Main items: KMS integration for keys, subnet routing and firewall rules for VPC peering, and disk performance for model artifacts. We'll share a runbook with prerequisites.
[20:10] Elena: For procurement we usually need a 30–60 day legal review. Any standard terms we should be aware of?
[20:16] Avery: We have an enterprise SLAs and a standard data processing addendum for PHI; we'll send draft terms for initial review.
[21:05] Marisol: Quick technical sidenote — do you have a preferred model family? That changes GPU sizing.
[21:11] Priya: We're evaluating open models; want to try a mix of a 13B quantized variant for short tasks and a 70B for heavy summarization. We'll provide sample prompts for both.
[21:40] Marisol: Perfect — we'll include both variants in the bench runs and measure tokens/sec and p95 for each.
[22:12] Marcus: Can Redwood support A/B routing between model versions? We want to do incremental rollouts.
[22:18] Marisol: Yes — rollouts, canary percentages, and automatic fallback policies are supported in the console.
[23:05] Priya: Any recommendations for cost-saving while preserving quality?

[23:10] Marisol: Use caching aggressively for repeated prefixes, adaptive batching, quantized variants for background tasks, and route long-running jobs to cheaper preemptible pools where latency isn't critical.
[24:01] Priya: Ok great. Let's talk deliverables and timing.

[24:08] Avery: Deliverables: 1) reserved capacity worksheet with baseline and burst scenarios, 2) SOC2 and Private runbook, 3) two-week PoC scope and benchmark plan. We'll aim to get the worksheet and security docs out by 2026-04-20. Benchmark can start once you send prompts — target to kick off 2026-04-22. Does that timeline work?
[24:35] Priya: Yes, that works for us.
[25:07] Elena: One more — do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for model encryption?
[25:12] Marisol: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations and BYOK are supported for Private and can be arranged for an enterprise Dedicated contract.
[26:00] Marcus: For the PoC, will we get logs with IP addresses? We have to redact PHI in logs.
[26:07] Avery: We can redact or mask payloads and configure retention. We'll include options in the runbook.
[27:30] Priya: If the benchmark looks good, what are typical lead times for reserved capacity?

[27:36] Avery: Provisioning a Dedicated pool typically takes 2–6 weeks depending on region and exact hardware. Private on-prem timelines vary more — usually 4–8 weeks including networking and security signoff.
[28:10] Priya: Ok noted. Any constraints on GPU types — do you offer multiple classes?
[28:16] Marisol: We offer A100-class equivalents, some H100 lanes in selected regions, and also smaller cards for cost-optimized tasks. We'll include hardware mappings in the worksheet.
[29:05] Marcus: For burst — can we reserve a cold pool that auto-starts only on demand?
[29:12] Marisol: Yes, cold pools with fast spin-up using pre-warm hooks. There is a warm-up window (tens of seconds) so for very tight p95 you need a small always-warm buffer.
[30:00] Elena: Are there partner references we can talk to?
[30:05] Avery: We'll share a shortlist — there are a few healthcare customers on Private deployments who have similar profiles.
[31:22] Priya: Great. Anything else we should call out?
[31:28] Marcus: On monitoring, we need per-tenant cost allocation. Will that be easy?
[31:34] Marisol: Yes — cost allocation at token level per-route/tenant is part of the console and we can dump reports to S3 or your billing system.
[32:05] Priya: Ok let's recap next steps.

[32:12] Avery: Recap: we'll send worksheet, benchmark plan, SOC2 + runbook by 2026-04-20; Shoreline will send sample prompts and select models by 2026-04-19; plan to start bench 2026-04-22. We'll also set up a short technical deep-dive during the PoC week for SREs.
[32:36] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[32:40] Avery: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and attachments. End call.
[32:46] [auto-generated note] Recording stopped.
